features.note: The abierta capture settles it: the opening shows a lit corridor floor, a back wall and a skirting, not a black rectangle and not a painted panel. The reveal lining reads on all three edges, so the hole is built rather than cut into cardboard. This is the single most likely way to build this asset wrong and it is right.

The horizontal bar crosses the leaf at 1.00 m with visible end brackets and a latch case at the leading stile. It is the one placement on this asset backed by evidence, and it is what makes the object read as an escape door rather than a lockable steel door.

The leaf swings outward, toward the viewer's side, and the hinge is on the far jamb, so the open leaf sits clear of the opening it reveals. The three hinges and the overhead closer are visible on the hinge stile in the open state.

The leaf reads as painted steel — flat, no metal glint — against the stainless bar and the kick plate, which do glint. Measured [120,141,160] at three independent points on the face, agreeing within one unit at deviation ~0; dE00 0 against the declared anchor.

The HUD carries SIN FICHA for the leaf dimensions and SIN RESOLVER for the bar-length rule with BOTH readings shown, in a warning colour distinct from the pass line. An asset built on inference says so on screen; that is the whole point of the policy under which it was authorised.

important_features.note: Green running-man sign above the opening, emissive so it reads as maintained. It answers WHY the door carries EN 1125 hardware.
1.8 m occupant beside the opening; the leaf reads as person-sized. Joints continuous — the floating-head defect from esclusa-personal was carried across as a fixed pattern rather than re-discovered.

defects: The leaf is deliberately plain: no vision panel, no louvre, no signage on the leaf itself. That is defensible for a security door but it means the hero read carries little detail below the bar, and formDetail scores accordingly.
The corridor beyond is a floor, a back wall and a skirting — enough to prove the opening is real, but it is scenery and does not pretend to be more.

Every leaf, frame and wall dimension is [INFER] at low confidence. The asset is honest about this on screen, but it remains a proportioned guess rather than a measured product, and global_min was lowered to 0.72 for that reason.

mechanical.note: Console-clean on all THREE capture sidecars plus a fourth clean run from probe-state driving btnDoor and btnWall. probe.mjs 30 draws / 1,806 tris against a budget of 40 / 200,000. No test suite, so tests is null. colorTarget anchored by projected geometry on the painted leaf, three independent points agreeing within one unit, dE00 0. AUTHORISATION: built under the datasheet-less policy the USER confirmed directly in this session's channel; an earlier relayed authorisation was declined as unverifiable, and only the non-policy-dependent evidence work (block121) was done in the interim. THREE DEFECTS CAUGHT BEFORE THIS REVIEW: (1) the opening revealed BLACK — the interior light added for exactly that purpose had no surface behind the hole to illuminate, so the corridor floor and back wall had to exist first; a lamp lighting nothing is not a fix. (2) The corridor's far wall poked into the HUD band; solved by projection (2.4 m -> ndcY 0.663 vs the main wall's 0.661; lowered to 2.2 m -> 0.600) rather than nudged by eye. (3) A SELF-INFLICTED regression: an sd text replacement swallowed `beyondWall.receiveShadow = true; wall.add(beyondWall);` into the comment it was inserting, silently removing the far wall from the scene. No console error and no failed check — the only signal was the draw count dropping 30 to 29 between two preflights. DEVIATIONS: the reviewer is the ORCHESTRATOR INLINE, not a fresh-context blind agent, so this verdict is a SELF-REVIEW; the neutral view is deliberately the default camera; no reference-match view exists (p6_comparison: spec-only).
